author: asukhobo
title: Debian Packages job fails - apt-get cannot resolve archive.ubuntu.com mirrors (DNS resolution failure)
signature: temporary failure resolving ubuntu archive mirror hosts during apt get update package has no installation candidate|Network

failed_jobs.name: Debian Packages / Debian Packages
failed_jobs.symptom: 'Install debian packages & check conflicts' step runs apt-get update, which fails to resolve archive.ubuntu.com, azure.archive.ubuntu.com and security.ubuntu.com, leaving gnupg/wget/ca-certificates/lsb-release uninstallable; apt-get install exits with code 100.

key_errors:
Err:1 http://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu noble InRelease
  Temporary failure resolving 'archive.ubuntu.com'

Err:3 http://azure.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu noble InRelease
  Temporary failure resolving 'azure.archive.ubuntu.com'

Err:2 http://security.ubuntu.com/ubuntu noble-security InRelease
  Temporary failure resolving 'security.ubuntu.com'

E: Package 'gnupg' has no installation candidate
E: Unable to locate package wget
E: Package 'ca-certificates' has no installation candidate
E: Unable to locate package lsb-release
root_cause: The 'Debian Packages' job's 'Install debian packages & check conflicts' step runs 'apt-get update -y' against the standard Ubuntu 24.04 (noble) mirrors (archive.ubuntu.com, azure.archive.ubuntu.com, security.ubuntu.com) before installing gnupg/wget/ca-certificates/lsb-release and the local openvino .deb package. All three mirror hostnames failed DNS resolution ('Temporary failure resolving') for roughly 4 minutes of retries (14:02:44 to 14:06:52), so apt's package index was never refreshed and the subsequent 'apt-get install' could not locate any of the requested packages, exiting with code 100. This is a transient DNS/network outage on the runner's resolver or network path, not a deterministic code or dependency problem; the PR's changed files (NPUW Whisper reset-state C++/test changes) do not touch the Debian packaging workflow or its dependencies and are unrelated to this failure.
reproduction_steps: N/A - not reliably reproducible locally; depends on hitting the same transient DNS/network outage on the GitHub-hosted runner. Re-running the failed 'Debian Packages' job alone is expected to succeed once DNS resolution recovers.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed 'Debian Packages' job; no code change is required since the PR's changes are unrelated to this failure.

If this recurs frequently, add the apt mirror hostnames to the workflow rerunner's known transient-failure strings (already proposed via propose_rerun_pattern in this run) so future occurrences are auto-rerun.

Consider adding a short retry/backoff wrapper around 'apt-get update' in the Debian Packages workflow step itself (in addition to the existing 'Acquire::Retries "10"' apt.conf, which only retries HTTP fetches, not DNS resolution failures) to better tolerate transient resolver outages.
prevention_strategies: Wrap 'apt-get update' invocations in CI with an explicit shell-level retry loop that also covers DNS failures (apt's own Acquire::Retries does not retry a failed DNS lookup cleanly within the same invocation), and/or pin a resilient DNS resolver (e.g., 1.1.1.1/8.8.8.8 fallback) on the runner image for apt operations.
historical_context: Repo-memory holds several related but distinct Network-category Debian Packages patterns keyed on 'Could not connect to azure.archive.ubuntu.com' (signature_hash 7d2e2ff59d37c6b4, seen 9 times as of 2026-08-19, and several single-occurrence variants such as 7d52cc57d8ed2a36, 98edf6d4fbc865bd, a3d456bd40bd9f42, c8d00529252cfb02, e65acb49deb19d88). Those record a TCP connection failure to the azure mirror specifically. This run's failure is a DNS resolution failure ('Temporary failure resolving') affecting all three configured mirrors simultaneously, which is a different underlying symptom, so a new pattern record was created rather than incrementing an existing one.
